prompts.text: Compare daily journal entries, topic notes and project notes for organizing a personal knowledge base. Give the strengths and trade-offs of each.
Summarise the raft project in this brain and identify its next concrete step.
Read the journal in this brain and explain one recurring theme, with evidence from the entries.
Help me choose between daily journal entries and topic notes. Explain the trade-off, then end your answer by asking me one question to decide between them.
Read the raft project in this brain. Explain the next decision, then end your answer by asking me one question about it.
Read the journal in this brain. Explain one recurring theme, then end your answer by asking me one question to reflect on it.

rule:
Render one structured block inline in your answer, at the point where you call it: a comparison table, stat tiles, a trend chart, a data table, a bar list, a receipt, a step list, a timeline, a schedule, a quote card, a contact card, a supporting-files list, a map of places, a small graph, an imported track, a link card or a list of tracker changes. One kind is the exception: suggestions is not drawn where you call it but under the finished answer.
files: local notes that support the answer, with optional plain-text reasons. Use exact brain-relative paths; reasons are your claims, not evidence that a file was read. Do not invent retrieval scores. Invalid or unavailable paths never authorize another destination.
graph: 2-20 nodes, at most 40 indexed edges. Supply labels, optional brain paths and one focus, never coordinates; only supplied relationships are drawn, duplicates are removed. This is your statement, not host-verified graph evidence.
If you are about to write a markdown table, stop and call this instead: kind=comparison when the columns are options the reader is choosing between, kind=table otherwise. A markdown table in this chat is a block that was not drawn.
The block IS part of the answer, so call it where the block belongs and write the prose around it; do not repeat the block's contents in prose, and do not draw the same thing as a markdown table. One or two blocks per answer; more than three is a dashboard, not an answer.
Values are strings you have already formatted with their unit and precision; the blocks do no arithmetic, no rounding and no currency. Keep labels short: they are read on a phone.
comparison: the reader is choosing between 2-4 options. Three columns fit a phone; use four only when the reader is on a wide screen. Mark at most one column recommended, and then give a footnote that states what the recommendation costs.
stats: 3-4 headline figures with a one-line meta each; they wrap in threes. trend: one figure over time, values oldest first, a delta pill only when there is a comparison. table: records with 2-6 columns, right-align numbers. bars: shares of a whole, pct 0-100; tone is the class of work (the same class draws the same colour on every chart), not a judgement of the row.
receipt: what a tool or a change did, as key/value rows, with a footnote for scope; a toned value fits one phone line at 25 characters (28 untoned) and wraps past it. steps: a procedure (numbered), things to tick off (checklist) or work being done for the reader (progress, exactly one current step).
timeline: what happened when, oldest first, pulse only on the one thing still happening. schedule: what is coming, grouped by day. quote: the exact words with a source and a locator, when the words themselves are the evidence. contact: a person, company or project with facts, when the answer is who.
map: 1-30 named places in reading order; the surface numbers them, draws them on real geography and lists every one under the map. Give lat/lon only when a source states them and name the source; list a place without them rather than estimating. You choose the places, never the zoom or the drawing.
track: a validated GPX, KML or supported GeoJSON attachment. Give only source.path from intake; the surface reads the original, calculates shared measurements and draws it without inferring recorded travel. Never restate coordinates or choose a viewport.
link: one external page the reader may want to open, with an absolute http(s) url and no user:password@. Brain shows its address and marks your title and description as yours; it never opens the page. A url that is relative, not http(s), carries credentials, or mixes alphabets in one part of its name is rejected with the reason.
tracker: issues and pull requests you just opened, closed, reopened, merged, labeled, commented on or reviewed, 1-20 events in the order you made them, each with the item's url, the action and its title. Use it instead of listing tracker changes in prose: each event is drawn as one tappable line that opens the item. Give closed its reason, labeled its label and reviewed its verdict as the qualifier. Never state the repository, number or type: they are read from a github.com url, and a field naming them is rejected. A url the link policy refuses is rejected with the reason, as for link.
suggestions: at most two follow-ups the reader would plausibly ask next, each grounded in this answer and phrased as the reader would type it; omit it when the answer ends by asking the reader something, and never add generic ones. Tapping one only puts it in the reader's composer to edit; it never sends. Call it last, at most once.
The tool has no side effect and returns what it was given; a rejected call means the block did not fit its schema, or a link's or tracker event's address was refused, so fix the shape or the address rather than retrying it unchanged.

note.description: A quiet mono line under the label: provenance, not a second value.

tone.description: One of the kit's accents, or "ink" (primary text) / "dim" (secondary text); omit for the default.

recommended.description: Tints the whole column. At most one column, and only with a footnote.

columns.description: The options being compared. Three fit a phone; four only on a wide screen.

tone.description: One of the kit's accents, or "ink" (primary text) / "dim" (secondary text); omit for the default.

cells.description: One cell per column, in column order. A string, or {v, tone} to colour it.

footnote.description: Why the recommendation is the recommendation, stated as a cost. Required when a column is recommended.

value.description: The figure, pre-formatted with its unit.

meta.description: A line under the value: the comparison or the period.

icon.description: A kit icon key such as "wallet", "calendar", "deadline", "ledger", "health", "link", "file", "agent". Omit when unsure: an unknown key is dropped.

tone.description: One of the kit's accents, or "ink" (primary text) / "dim" (secondary text); omit for the default.

tiles.description: Headline figures. Three or four read best; they wrap in threes on a phone.

label.description: The uppercase mono line above the number.

value.description: The headline figure, pre-formatted. The chart does no arithmetic.

delta.description: The change pill, e.g. "+12%" or "−3 days". Omit when there is no comparison.

deltaTone.description: "teal" for a good change, "red" for a bad one.

values.description: The series in its own unit, oldest first. Scaled against its own maximum.

ticks.description: One label per bucket; empty strings are unlabelled slots. Same length as values.

tone.description: One of the kit's accents; omit for the default.
One of the kit's accents; omit for the default.

cells.description: One cell per column, in column order.

value.description: The figure shown beside the bar, pre-formatted.

tone.description: The class of work this row is, not a judgement of it; the same class draws the same colour on every chart. Omit for the default.

rows.description: Shares of a whole, largest first unless the order means something.

title.description: The uppercase mono header. Omit for a bare row list.

titleIcon.description: A kit icon key such as "wallet", "calendar", "deadline", "ledger", "health", "link", "file", "agent". Omit when unsure: an unknown key is dropped.

titleTone.description: One of the kit's accents; omit for the default.

tone.description: One of the kit's accents, or "ink" (primary text) / "dim" (secondary text); omit for the default.

diff.description: A unified diff, rendered inset under the rows.

footnote.description: The scope line: what this receipt covers.

meta.description: A short right-aligned note: a duration, a place.

code.description: A mono line under the detail: a command, a bearing.

variant.description: numbered = a recipe to follow, checklist = things to tick off, progress = something being done for the reader.

tone.description: One of the kit's accents; omit for the default.

pulse.description: Reserved for the one event still happening.

meta.description: A note beside the day: a count, a place.

tag.description: A small pill. "conflict" is drawn gold.

tone.description: One of the kit's accents; omit for the default.

groups.description: What is coming, grouped by day.

source.description: Whose words: a document title, a person, a page.

locator.description: Line or section, so the reader can check it.

tone.description: Provenance colour; omit for the default.

icon.description: A kit icon key such as "wallet", "calendar", "deadline", "ledger", "health", "link", "file", "agent". Omit when unsure: an unknown key is dropped.

role.description: What they are to the reader, or their title.

contactKind.description: Decides the avatar shape and the default colour.

badge.description: A soft chip beside the name: standing, not status.

tone.description: The entity colour; omit for the kind's default.

facts.description: Key-value facts: last contact, company, city.

tone.description: One of the kit's accents, or "ink" (primary text) / "dim" (secondary text); omit for the default.

initials.description: Derived from the label when absent.

path.description: The exact brain-relative file path; never an external URL.

reason.description: Why this note supports the answer, as your own claim; plain text, not a retrieval score.

items.description: One to twenty supporting notes in the order the reader should inspect them.

title.description: What the set is: 'Where the crew went ashore'.

label.description: The place's name. Wraps; never cut.

meta.description: A short fact: a time, a day, a count.

source.description: Where you got the position: a note path, a document.

accuracyM.description: How sure the position is, in metres, if a source says so. Omit rather than guess.

places.description: In the order the reader should read them; the numbers follow this order. A place with no known position goes in WITHOUT lat/lon; never estimate one.

path.description: Optional brain-relative file link; refused destinations are plain text.

tone.description: One of the kit's accents; omit for the default.
One of the kit's accents; omit for the default.

path.description: The staged track file path returned by attachment intake. The surface reads this file; do not restate its coordinates.

title.description: A short title. Source provenance and measurements come from the file.

url.description: The absolute http(s) address, exactly as the reader should open it. No user:password@. Brain does not open or check it.

title.description: What the page is, in your words. Plain text; shown as written by you.

description.description: One or two sentences on why it is relevant. Plain text; shown as written by you.

url.description: The item's absolute https address, e.g. https://github.com/<owner>/<name>/issues/<n> or .../pull/<n>. Repository, number and type are read from it; never state them.

action.description: What you did to the item.

qualifier.description: A short note on the action: the close reason ("completed", "not planned", "duplicate"), the label name, or the review verdict ("approved", "changes requested"). Omit otherwise.

title.description: The item's title, one line. Shown as written by you, truncated to the line.

events.description: The changes in the order you made them. 1-20.

label.description: The uppercase mono line above the chips. Omit for the default, "Ask next".
The follow-up as the reader would type it; one line, at most 80 characters.

icon.description: A kit icon key such as "wallet", "calendar", "deadline", "ledger", "health", "link", "file", "agent". Omit when unsure: an unknown key is dropped.

items.description: One or two follow-ups grounded in this answer.
